newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's new oil money to pay old debt - minister.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's new oil money to pay old debt - minister.

text.p: Venezuela's windfall oil revenues, thanks to higher-than expected crude prices, will be used to meet outstanding debt payments, Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Thursday.
"I think we should administer these resources for the country's development and not so that it weakens," Arrieta told reporters at Miraflores presidential palace.

Referring to the total oil revenues of the past two decades, Arrieta said: "The $265 billion which was frittered away in the 20 years of this oil frenzy have left us this tremendous debt. Let us hope we can pay it to leave future generations free."
Venezuela has a foreign debt of about $35 billion.
A recent strengthening in oil prices, partly due to renewed tension in the Middle East, will see about $2.5 billion more oil revenues this year than had been expected just a few weeks ago.

The extra revenues are to be placed in a special fund created by the government to pay off outstanding debt, Arrieta said. Emerging country debt traders expect Venezuela to use part of the fund to buy back some of its $17.5 billion Brady bond debt.
The average price of Venezuela's basket of crudes and products is averaging $17.34 per barrel for the year so far, well up on an early forecast of $13.50 per barrel.
State oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) vice- President Claus Graf said the company would shortly present a new oil price estimate to replace the $15.60 per barrel average forecast recently.
Graf said the new estimate would be about $16.20 to $16.50 per barrel.
